walkthroughs.body_html:
Themes in Economics — a core area of A-Level Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Themes in Economics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Themes in Economics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CPI and RPI as inflation measures?
options: Both measure price changes via a basket of goods, but RPI includes housing costs (mortgage interest) and uses an arithmetic mean; CPI excludes housing costs and uses a geometric mean — CPI is the official UK target measure.
Opportunity cost is the money price of something.
CPI measures consumer prices and RPI measures retail prices — that's the only difference.
CPI and RPI always give the same inflation figure.
